title: Save and reload a local tokenizer
summary: A tokenizer can save its settings as a JSON file. Reloading that file restores the local vocabulary and processing rules.
introduction: A tokenizer can save its settings as a JSON file. Reloading that file restores the local vocabulary and processing rules. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain save and reload a local tokenizer
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A tokenizer can save its settings as a JSON file. Reloading that file restores the local vocabulary and processing rules.

blocks.code:
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
from tokenizers.models import WordLevel
from tokenizers.pre_tokenizers import Whitespace

tokenizer = Tokenizer(WordLevel({"[PAD]": 0, "[UNK]": 1, "moon": 2, "glows": 3}, unk_token="[UNK]"))
tokenizer.pre_tokenizer = Whitespace()
tokenizer.save("practice-tokenizer.json")
restored = Tokenizer.from_file("practice-tokenizer.json")
print(restored.encode("moon glows").ids)
blocks.title: Save and reload a local tokenizer

blocks.text: The output is [2, 3]. The local file stores the tokenizer setup. No model weights are trained, and nothing is uploaded to the Hub.
